title: Fisherman's rib fingerless mitts
subtitle: Thick, squishy fingerless mitts in fisherman's rib, worked in the round.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in DK wool worked in fisherman's rib, which produces a thick fabric similar to brioche without the complexity. Afterthought thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Fisherman's rib (knit 1 below) is documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) and appears in multiple UK knitting manuals from the early-to-mid 20th century, all out of UK and EU copyright. This fingerless mitt adaptation is a standard construction.

knitting.gaugeText: 20 sts x 28 rounds = 10 x 10 cm in fisherman's rib on 4 mm needles. The stitch creates a very elastic fabric; measure with the fabric relaxed.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern that creates a thick, double-layered fabric by knitting into the stitch below rather than the stitch on the needle. Worked in the round by alternating k1-below with purl stitches. The result looks like brioche rib but uses a single yarn and a simpler method.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in DK wool worked in
fisherman's rib
with an
afterthought thumb
. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

Fisherman's rib is worked in the round on an even number of stitches. On every round, alternate k1-below with purl. The k1-below stitch is knitted into the stitch one row down rather than into the stitch on the needle; the current-row stitch is then dropped. The double-layered fabric that results is springy, warm, and reversible. The construction uses
magic loop
on a long circular. Budget about 90 g (200 m / 220 yards) of DK wool per pair. Use 4 mm needles rather than the standard 3.75 mm because fisherman's rib knits at a looser row gauge.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 90 g (about 200 m / 220 yards) of DK-weight wool

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable, for magic loop

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 2: 1 for beginning of round, 1 for thumb position

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 25 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: Gauge
20 stitches and 28 rounds to 10 cm in fisherman's rib on 4 mm needles. Measure the swatch slightly stretched. The stitch count seems lower than standard DK but the fabric is thick; this is correct.
Fisherman's rib in the round

items.name: Setup round
items.qty: *k1, p1*; repeat to end. Work this round once only before beginning the pattern.

items.name: Pattern round
items.qty: *k1 below (knit into the stitch one row down, dropping the current stitch), p1*; repeat to end.

content.text: Every round is the same after the setup round. The k1-below inserts the right needle tip into the stitch directly below the stitch on the needle, knits it, and lets both the old stitch and the current stitch drop from the left needle together.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches, all even numbers. Join to work in the round. Work the setup round once, then work the pattern round for 28 (30, 32) rounds. The cuff measures about 10 (11, 11) cm.
Hand and thumb

Continue in fisherman's rib for 10 (12, 12) rounds. Place the thumb: work the first 9 (10, 11) stitches with waste yarn in the fisherman's rib pattern, slip back, and work them in pattern to end. Continue for 18 (20, 22) more rounds. Bind off in 1x1 rib.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn. Pick up 9 (10, 11) stitches above and 9 (10, 11) below. Work 14 (16, 16) rounds of fisherman's rib. Bind off in 1x1 rib.
Common faults
Stitch count grows: the current stitch on the needle was not dropped after the k1-below. Both the current stitch and the k1-below result must come off the left needle as one unit.

Fabric is plain 1x1 rib rather than double-layered: the k1-below was worked into the current stitch rather than into the row below. Insert the needle one row lower and check visually that the needle passes through a stitch from the previous round.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. The fisherman's rib fabric is both sides equally attractive.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry. The thick fabric takes longer to dry than a standard DK mitt.
What to try next

Two-colour brioche rib uses a similar double-layer construction but with two separate yarns for a richer colour effect. The brioche fingerless mitts pattern uses the same needle size and stitch count.
